tldr: This thread is a topical grouping of 28 arXiv preprints since Oct 26, not one event: what they share is reinforcement learning as a post-training method for LLMs and agents. Most of them work on one of three problems: what the reward should measure, how to train multi-turn tool-using agents, and how to pay for the rollouts.
whats_new: Two Nov 12 preprints close the window: StateAlign reports that RL tool-use gains can coincide with more tool hallucination and trains state-aware tool decisions, and a third rollout-scheduling paper coordinates inference with environment execution.
why_it_matters: For teams that post-train their own agents, these papers flag three costs: rollout scheduling as an infrastructure problem, reward design, and RL tool-use gains that can bring more tool hallucination.

beats.headline: Outcome-only rewards draw six papers on calibration, credit and guidance
beats.summary: These papers change what the policy is rewarded for: abstaining, matching confidence to correctness, or using the textual feedback a single outcome score discards.

beats.headline: RL moves onto the agent stack: harnesses, skills, memory and sub-agents
beats.summary: Eleven papers apply RL to parts of an agent system rather than to a single-turn model; one asks what multi-turn RL actually improves, and one targets the tool hallucination RL can introduce.

beats.headline: Three papers treat rollout scheduling as the bottleneck
beats.summary: Environment-aware scheduling on Oct 27, an offline scheduler for asynchronous LLM RL on Nov 6, and inference-environment coordination on Nov 12.

beats.headline: Eight clustered papers sit outside LLM agent post-training
beats.summary: Diffusion and flow fine-tuning, classical RL interpretability and theory, and two agent papers on voice benchmarks and shared-memory coordination.

open_questions: Do any of the three rollout-scheduling approaches ship as open-source code or get adopted in a public training stack?
Does an independent group reproduce the finding that multi-turn RL gains depend on sampling breadth and interaction depth?
Do the confidence-calibration methods for RLVR hold on agent tasks, beyond the RAG and reasoning settings they were proposed for?
Does co-evolving the harness with the policy beat tuning a harness for a fixed policy on a shared public benchmark?
Does state-aware RL training cut tool hallucination without giving back the task-success gains, on a public multi-turn tool benchmark?
take_for_builders: Before adding GPUs to an agent RL pipeline, measure how much rollout wall-clock goes to environment execution and padding; after any RL tool-use tune, track tool-hallucination rate alongside task success.

day_captions.65dc6916d3b352f1: Off the agent track: how to inject stochasticity so GRPO can train few-step flow models.
day_captions.4e3ef058b96b399d: Classical RL interpretability: explains agent policies through causal graph reasoning.
day_captions.473a95cd7c540d1a: Trains a prompt compressor with a mix of RL and supervised learning, aimed at cheaper and faster LLM calls.
day_captions.bce25dc1c825a3e7: Theory entry: an axiomatic basis for RL when only a subset of agents is controllable, with smart grids as the motivating domain.
day_captions.3ac08f6799c57341: Uses RL to close the gap between HTML that renders and HTML that works and looks right under real interaction.
day_captions.08c314bb237b4b82: Hierarchical multi-agent RL for long-horizon, multi-step tasks in GUI web agents.
day_captions.d97ee2168f669bce: Addresses on-policy RL stalling when the base model cannot reach the reward, using guidance drawn from textual reward sources such as judge models.
day_captions.219537f3fa2b3690: Moves skill memory out of the prompt and into the model by combining RL with on-policy self-distillation.
day_captions.981c5fba5d1f60bf: Multi-agent RL for sub-agents that explore in parallel with isolated context windows.
day_captions.4553deeec0e06574: The thread's diagnostic paper: multi-turn RL gains are highly sensitive to sampling breadth and interaction depth.

day_captions.6fd3ac39e855936d: Model-based RL entry on encoding memory in world models at test time.
day_captions.f5f5bfe9b72425ef: A benchmark with no RL method: task coordination in full-duplex voice agents, where users interrupt and redirect mid-speech.
day_captions.29f0e99816524f78: A replication study with no RL method: whether LLM agents coordinate through shared memory without being told to.
day_captions.84ecbe8e1def5e6c: Trains incremental summarization with RL so bounded agent memory is optimized for downstream task utility.
day_captions.283f892f9c4f657a: Adds AI-chosen training-time hints to RLVR, on the argument that an outcome reward reduces each attempt to a single number.
day_captions.a7b79c5f448ee3b6: Classical RL interpretability for high-dimensional multi-action policies.
day_captions.e372c76cd210406f: Third scheduling paper: coordinates LLM inference with environment execution to cut batch makespan for evals, synthetic data and RL rollouts.
